groups.title: Assets
groups.description: Resources controlled by the business and amounts owed TO it. Assets normally increase with a debit (Dr).

accounts.name: Bank
accounts.meaning: Money held in the business bank account.
accounts.clues: Cash received, paid into bank, paid from bank. Only use Bank if money actually moves. An overdraft is different: see Liabilities.

accounts.name: Trade receivables
accounts.meaning: Customers owe the business for goods or services already supplied on credit.
accounts.clues: Sold on credit; customer will pay later. A later receipt reduces this asset, not a second sale.

accounts.name: Equipment cost
accounts.meaning: The original cost of long-term equipment or vehicles used by the business.
accounts.clues: Buy a computer, van or equipment for business use, not to resell. Not an immediate running expense.

accounts.name: Prepayments
accounts.meaning: A benefit already paid for but not yet used.
accounts.clues: Insurance or rent paid in advance; some months relate to next year. The unused portion is an asset, not this year's expense.

accounts.name: Accrued income
accounts.meaning: Income already earned but not yet received or recorded.
accounts.clues: Service already performed; interest earned but not received. The business has a right to collect.

accounts.name: Loan receivable
accounts.meaning: Principal owed to this business because it lent money to someone else.
accounts.clues: The business lends money; another entity repays a loan we made. Different from money WE borrowed.

accounts.name: Investment
accounts.meaning: Funds invested by the business to earn a return.
accounts.clues: Business buys an investment in another entity. The original investment is an asset; dividend or interest income is separate.

accounts.name: Accumulated depreciation
accounts.meaning: A contra-asset: depreciation charged to date, deducted from the related asset's cost.
accounts.clues: Total depreciation so far; transfer the sold asset's accumulated depreciation. Grouped with assets because it REDUCES their carrying amount. Its normal credit balance does not make it a liability.

accounts.name: Inventory
accounts.meaning: Goods still held, normally at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
accounts.clues: Unsold goods, units on hand, stock left at year-end. Purchases is a different account in this site's periodic system.

accounts.name: Raw materials
accounts.meaning: Manufacturing inventory not yet used in production.
accounts.clues: Materials held ready to make goods.

accounts.name: Work in progress
accounts.meaning: Manufacturing inventory that is only partly completed.
accounts.clues: Part-finished goods at year-end.

accounts.name: Finished goods
accounts.meaning: Completed manufactured goods not yet sold.
accounts.clues: Ready to sell but still held. Raw materials, work in progress and finished goods are components of inventory: do not count them again on top of its total.

groups.title: Capital / Equity
groups.description: The owner's residual interest: assets less liabilities. Contributions increase equity; drawings and distributions reduce it without being expenses.

accounts.name: Capital
accounts.meaning: Funding contributed by the owner.
accounts.clues: Owner invests savings, starts the business with funds, introduces capital. Not sales revenue and not a repayable loan.

accounts.name: Drawings
accounts.meaning: A sole trader's withdrawals for personal use; a deduction from equity.
accounts.clues: Owner takes money for personal shopping or living costs. Not wages, rent or another business expense. Drawings increase with a debit because they reduce equity.

accounts.name: Dividends (equity distribution)
accounts.meaning: A company distribution to shareholders, reducing equity.
accounts.clues: Company pays a dividend to its owners. Not an expense and not the same as dividend income earned on an investment. If a dividend payable was already recorded, its payment clears that liability instead.

accounts.name: Retained earnings
accounts.meaning: Cumulative company profits retained after distributions and other relevant movements.
accounts.clues: Opening retained profit plus this year's profit, less dividends. A loss reduces it; an accumulated deficit can have a debit balance.

accounts.name: Ordinary shares
accounts.meaning: The nominal amount of ordinary share capital issued by a company.
accounts.clues: A company issues ordinary ownership shares. Share capital is not sales.

accounts.name: Share premium
accounts.meaning: Amounts subscribed for shares above their nominal value.
accounts.clues: Issue price exceeds nominal value; the excess belongs to equity, not revenue.

groups.title: Liabilities
groups.description: Obligations: amounts the business owes, or goods/services it must still provide. Liabilities normally increase with a credit (Cr).

accounts.name: Trade payables
accounts.meaning: Amounts owed to suppliers for goods or services received on credit.
accounts.clues: Buy on credit; supplier invoice outstanding. Paying an existing invoice reduces the payable rather than recording the purchase again.

accounts.name: Accruals
accounts.meaning: Costs already incurred but not yet paid or recorded; in these exercises, often not yet billed.
accounts.clues: Used but not yet billed, paid or recorded; a missing year-end expense. Record the expense AND the obligation. Different from accrued income, which is an asset.

accounts.name: Income received in advance
accounts.meaning: Customer money received before the promised goods or services have been provided.
accounts.clues: Customer pays now for next year; service still owed. It is not revenue yet. Different from a prepaid EXPENSE, which is an asset.

accounts.name: Loan payable
accounts.meaning: Borrowed principal the business must repay.
accounts.clues: The business borrows or receives a bank loan. Repaying principal reduces this liability; interest is a separate expense.

accounts.name: Warranty provision
accounts.meaning: An estimated liability for the cost of meeting warranty obligations.
accounts.clues: Expected claims on goods already sold; claim rate times average repair cost. Payment of a covered claim uses the provision.

accounts.name: Deferred grant income
accounts.meaning: Grant receipts not yet recognised as income under the deferral model assumed in the exercises.
accounts.clues: Grant covers future costs or several years. Release the matching part to Grant income when the stated conditions are met.

accounts.name: Bank (overdraft)
accounts.meaning: A negative bank balance: money owed to the bank.
accounts.clues: Payments exceed available funds; the exercise explicitly says overdraft. This is a credit balance in Bank, not a new account to select in the journal builder.

groups.title: Revenue / Income
groups.description: Amounts earned by the business, increasing profit and hence equity. Income normally increases with a credit (Cr). Cash receipts alone do not prove income was earned.

accounts.name: Sales
accounts.meaning: Revenue from goods or services supplied to customers.
accounts.clues: Sold goods for cash or on credit. A customer settling an old debt is not another sale.

accounts.name: Service income
accounts.meaning: Revenue earned by providing a service.
accounts.clues: Work completed, services performed or fees earned. Receiving payment before performance may instead create income in advance.

accounts.name: Interest income
accounts.meaning: The return earned on money lent or deposited.
accounts.clues: Receive or earn interest on a loan made to someone else. The return of the original principal clears Loan receivable instead.

accounts.name: Dividend income
accounts.meaning: A return earned on the business's investment in shares.
accounts.clues: The business receives a dividend from another company. Different from a dividend this business pays to its own owners.

accounts.name: Grant income
accounts.meaning: The portion of a grant recognised as income under the stated exercise assumptions.
accounts.clues: Qualifying costs incurred; release the year's portion of a deferred grant. Check conditions: not every grant cash receipt is immediate income.

accounts.name: Gain on disposal
accounts.meaning: Proceeds from an asset disposal exceeding its carrying amount.
accounts.clues: Sell a non-current asset for more than its net book value. This is other income/gain, not ordinary trading sales; only the gain affects profit.

groups.title: Expenses
groups.description: Costs consumed in earning this period's income, reducing profit. Expenses normally increase with a debit (Dr), even if not yet paid.

accounts.name: Purchases
accounts.meaning: Goods bought for resale under this site's periodic inventory system.
accounts.clues: Buy resale goods, for cash or on credit. Do not use for equipment, rent or every purchase in everyday language. Unsold inventory is removed from cost of sales at year-end.

accounts.name: Depreciation expense
accounts.meaning: This period's allocation of a non-current asset's depreciable cost.
accounts.clues: Annual depreciation charge; asset used during the year. Credit Accumulated depreciation, not Bank.

accounts.name: Rent expense
accounts.meaning: Cost of using premises during this period.
accounts.clues: Rent relating to the current year, whether paid or accrued. Unused future rent belongs in Prepayments.

accounts.name: Insurance expense
accounts.meaning: Insurance cover used during this period.
accounts.clues: Months of cover relating to the current year. Paid but unused cover is a Prepayment.

accounts.name: Electricity expense
accounts.meaning: Electricity consumed by the business during this period.
accounts.clues: Electricity has been used, including an unbilled year-end estimate. Use Accruals as the other account if unpaid and unrecorded; Bank only if actually paid.

accounts.name: Interest expense
accounts.meaning: The business's cost of borrowing, separate from principal repayment.
accounts.clues: Interest charged on our loan; interest part of an instalment. Not the entire loan repayment.

accounts.name: Grants paid expense
accounts.meaning: A straightforward grant or charitable donation paid out with nothing directly in return.
accounts.clues: Business gives a donation, not an owner withdrawing money. Different from Grant income.

accounts.name: Warranty expense
accounts.meaning: Expected warranty cost recognised for obligations from past sales.
accounts.clues: Recognise or top up an expected warranty provision. A claim covered by an existing provision reduces that provision instead of charging the same expense again.

accounts.name: Loss on disposal
accounts.meaning: The shortfall when disposal proceeds are below the asset's carrying amount.
accounts.clues: Sell a non-current asset for less than its net book value. Recognise only the loss, not all original cost as a new expense.

accounts.name: Cost of sales
accounts.meaning: Cost of the inventory actually sold during the period.
accounts.clues: Opening inventory plus purchases less closing inventory in the simple periodic model. Not the selling price and not all goods bought.

accounts.name: Wages expense
accounts.meaning: Staff wages earned during this period.
accounts.clues: Employee work already done; include unpaid amounts relating to this year.

accounts.name: Utilities expense
accounts.meaning: A broader running-cost label for services such as electricity, gas and water.
accounts.clues: Utility services consumed. Where the exercise offers the specific Electricity expense account, use that specific name.

specialAccounts.name: Disposal
specialAccounts.meaning: A temporary clearing account, not a permanent asset, liability, equity, income or expense account.
specialAccounts.clues: On sale of a non-current asset: collect original cost (Dr), accumulated depreciation (Cr) and proceeds (Cr). A remaining Dr is a loss; a remaining Cr is a gain. Transfer that result to Loss on disposal or Gain on disposal, leaving Disposal at nil.
